clue.text: H in an isolated location

parts.note: the letter H sits in the very centre of the seven-letter word nowhere
the surface reading: something stranded far from anywhere

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the clue says where the letter H is: in the centre of the word 'nowhere'. The same phrase names a remote spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a remote place far from towns or people, which is what an isolated location is.

clue.text: Swab around half of thin housetop made of cedar, perhaps

indicators.note: the swab word goes round the half-word, which sits inside it

parts.note: a mop
the first two of its four letters
roof, the top of a house

explanation.surface: Mopping round a thin roof made of cedar shingles.
explanation.walkthrough: Cedar wood repels clothes moths, which is why chests and closets are lined with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cedar's natural oils deter fabric-eating insects, so cedar storage resists them; the 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: Delaware and outside of Delaware — that doesn't go anywhere

indicators.note: the word and is put outside the second Delaware, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Delaware and the land beyond it are described as going nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: DE is the US postal abbreviation for Delaware.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead end is a road or plan with no way through, leading nowhere.

clue.text: Minimum ale a stein can hold

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them, spanning their letters

parts.note: the answer runs across these three words, from the end of ale into stein

explanation.surface: The smallest amount of beer a beer mug can contain.
explanation.definitionFit: Least is the smallest amount possible, the lowest quantity.

clue.text: Best (or sunniest, at first) setting for a picnic

parts.note: to best someone is to outdo them
taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of sunniest is taken

parts.note: only its opening S is used

explanation.surface: Choosing the finest, or the brightest, spot for a picnic.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnic is a meal eaten in the open air, away from buildings.

clue.text: Insult pierces fanatic person who scorns any cover-up?

indicators.note: the insult goes into the fanatic word, as a blade pierces something

parts.note: a nut, an obsessive enthusiast
dis, slang for disrespect

explanation.surface: A jibe wounds a zealot who rails against conspiracies and cover-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover-up suggests political scandal; the question mark warns it means clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes without clothes, rejecting anything that conceals the body.

clue.text: She twirls exotically in some American paintings

indicators.note: in an unusual, foreign fashion, so the letters are rearranged strangely

parts.note: these nine letters are the raw material to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dancer spins in an exotic way within some American artworks.
explanation.definitionFit: James McNeill Whistler was an American painter; his works are called by his name.

clue.text: Expedition's leader in back of the boat, facing sunrise

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

parts.note: supplies only its opening E
astern, at or toward the rear of a vessel

explanation.surface: An explorer sits at the stern looking toward the dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun rises in the east, so eastern means oriented toward dawn.

clue.text: Former team's unfinished revelation

indicators.note: the revelation is left incomplete, losing its final letter

parts.note: a journalistic piece that lays bare a scandal, borrowed from French

explanation.surface: A defunct team's story is told incompletely.
explanation.walkthrough: The Montreal Expos were a Major League Baseball team that moved to Washington in 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: The Expos were a baseball club that no longer exists under that name.

clue.text: Milk producer adopts vehicle — it might roll by around 4:00

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the teat takes the car inside itself

parts.note: a teat is what milk comes out of
a car is the everyday vehicle

explanation.surface: A dairy cow takes on a vehicle that trundles past in the late afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 4:00 is teatime, when a wheeled trolley of tea might be pushed round.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wheeled trolley for serving afternoon refreshments is pushed around at teatime, roughly four o'clock.

clue.text: Embracing contrary practice, dullard runs out

indicators.note: the dullard's word holds the other piece in its arms, so it goes round it

parts.note: a drip is a feeble, boring person

indicators.note: contrary means turned the opposite way, so the word for practice is read backwards

parts.note: use as in custom or habit

explanation.surface: A dull person, faced with a habit they dislike, flees the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply that dwindles to nothing is said to dry up, the same as being exhausted.

clue.text: Provided piece of eggplant as ingredient for soup, stirred in ample quantity

indicators.note: an ingredient goes into a dish, so these pieces are put inside the stirred soup
stirring mixes things up, so the letters of soup are rearranged

parts.note: its four letters are the base that gets stirred
lent, as in given for a while

indicators.note: a small piece here is just the opening letter of the word

parts.note: supplies only its opening E

explanation.surface: A recipe note: the eggplant was added to the soup and stirred in generously.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means plentiful or abundant, existing in large amounts.

clue.text: Peg's clutching part of rug — what might prevent you from seeing 18

definitions.text: what might prevent you from seeing 18
definitions.note: plural answer for 'what': the idiom is not seeing the wood for the trees

indicators.note: to clutch is to hold tight, so the peg word holds the letter inside

parts.note: a tee is a golf peg; the 's adds the S

indicators.note: only a fragment of the word is used: its opening letter

parts.note: supplies only its opening R

explanation.surface: A tent peg snags on a rug, getting in the way of seeing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 across is FOREST: the idiom 'can't see the forest for the trees' means being lost in detail.
explanation.definitionFit: In the saying, the individual plants block the view of the whole woodland they make up.

clue.text: In bishop's absence, fearless legionnaire's head is wrapped in bloodstained flag

indicators.note: together with absence: with the bishop gone, his letter is removed
the bishop is absent, so his letter is dropped from the fearless word

parts.note: bold, as in brave
B is the chess notation for a bishop

indicators.note: the head letter is enclosed by the bloodstained word as if in a wrapping

parts.note: gory, covered in blood

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: supplies only its opening L

explanation.surface: A battlefield scene: a brave legionnaire, with no bishop present, is wrapped in a bloody banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Glory is the nickname of the United States national banner, the Stars and Stripes.

clue.text: Endure Los Angeles with expression of disgust — that's what winners get

parts.note: last, as in survive or keep going
ugh, a grunt of revulsion

explanation.surface: Putting up with LA and groaning about it is the victor's reward.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says whoever triumphs in the end has the final laugh at their doubters.

clue.text: By the sound of it, passes out tricks

indicators.note: tells us the answer sounds like the word for passing out, though spelt differently

parts.note: faints, loses consciousness

explanation.surface: Someone collapses, or perhaps just pretends to, as a ploy.
explanation.definitionFit: Feints are deceptive moves or bluffs meant to mislead an opponent.

clue.text: Execute one curve in reverse, as part of the marching band

indicators.note: the whole string is read from the back

parts.note: murder, kill
an, the indefinite article
an S is shaped like a curve

explanation.surface: A drill instruction: perform one turn backwards as part of a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare is the sharp-sounding drum carried in marching bands.

clue.text: Herb crashed into Carl

indicators.note: something crashed is wrecked, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: these eight letters are the raw material to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Herb drove into a man named Carl.
explanation.walkthrough: Herb looks like a man's name, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cilantro is the American name for coriander leaves, a kitchen herb.

clue.text: Wood that's most in favor?

parts.note: for, as in supporting
-est is the suffix that makes the superlative, the most of something

explanation.surface: A question about which timber is the favorite.
explanation.walkthrough: The superlative suffix -est is what turns an adjective into its 'most' form.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood is a tract of land covered with trees, a woodland.

clue.text: Convert or alter a sphere

indicators.note: to alter is to change, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: these seven letters are the raw material to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to transform or modify a globe.
explanation.definitionFit: To reshape something is to change its form, which is to convert it.

clue.text: Family spoiled Sasha in nation's capital

parts.note: kin, one's relatives

indicators.note: spoiled means ruined, so the letters of the name are messed up

parts.note: the name's five letters are the raw material to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A family pampers a girl named Sasha in a national capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Sasha is one of the Obama daughters, which feeds the picture of a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinshasa is the capital city of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

clue.text: Bening's stake holding trap

definitions.note: possessive phrasing for a first name: Bening's is Annette

indicators.note: the stake word holds the trap inside it

parts.note: an ante is a gambler's stake
a net traps animals

explanation.surface: An actress's poker stake contains a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: Annette Bening is an American film actress, so 'Bening's' first name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Annette is the given name of the Hollywood actress Bening, who starred in American Beauty.

clue.text: Quiet GI's negative response: "Back in the brig"

parts.note: p is piano, the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: back means turned backwards, so the soldier's reply is reversed

parts.note: a soldier refusing says no sir

explanation.surface: A soldier quietly says no and is sent back to the military jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The brig is naval slang for a ship's jail, a place of confinement.

clue.text: Repair a slab at the foundation

indicators.note: to repair is to fix up, so the letters are rearranged into working order

parts.note: these five letters are the raw material to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A builder's note: mend a concrete slab at a building's base.
explanation.definitionFit: Basal means forming or belonging to the base, the bottom layer of something.

clue.text: Clinton's notes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: belonging to Bill, the former US president

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive reads as a politician's jottings; read it as Bill's and it matches the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Bills are paper currency, and Bill's is the president's first name with the possessive.

clue.text: Change the configuration of back burner?

parts.note: rear, the back part
a range is a cooking stove with burners

explanation.surface: Asks whether moving the pan to the back hob counts as reorganising the stove.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'back burner' is a stove's rear ring; split, it is back plus a cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange something is to alter its layout or arrangement.

clue.text: Strict truck driver's license?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a non-articulated truck, the kind such a license covers

explanation.walkthrough: A rigid truck is one whose cab and body are one unit, unlike an articulated rig; licenses are graded by which kind you may drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means stiff and exacting, and also names a single-chassis lorry.

clue.text: Associations with the French contracting disease

indicators.note: contracting reads as catching an illness, but here the French article holds the disease inside it

parts.note: les is the French plural for the
ague is an old name for a malarial fever

explanation.surface: Societies linked with the French catch an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracting' looks like catching a disease, and it is, as an insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Leagues are alliances or organised groups of clubs, nations or members.

clue.text: Boxer, switching truth value, gets more drunk

indicators.note: true and false are logic's T and F, so the boxer's F is swapped for T

parts.note: a fighter, someone who fights in the ring

explanation.surface: A boxer who changes his story gets drunker.
explanation.walkthrough: In logic, truth values are written T and F, so flipping one turns the F into a T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is slang for drunk or intoxicated, so the comparative means drunker.

clue.text: Composer with spouse's child eating chicken — he is in shadowy surroundings

indicators.note: the stepson swallows the chicken, so it goes inside

parts.note: a stepson is the son of your husband or wife
a hen is a chicken

indicators.note: with surroundings: he sits inside the shadowy word
the shadowy word surrounds the pronoun he

parts.note: dim, poorly lit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer and his stepson eat chicken while sitting in a dim room.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Sondheim was the American writer of music and lyrics for Sweeney Todd and Company.
